messages:
Priya Shah: Quick heads-up — Acme is insisting on guaranteed persistent public egress IPs for their private deployment. Sales wants us to commit this in the PRD and contract.
Ryan Kim: Clarify scope please: do they want stable NAT IPs we own, or BGP advertising of their prefixes from our edge?
Priya Shah: They want both options: (1) Redwood-managed static IPv4 egress IPs that don’t change across upgrades, and (2) optional BGP advertise-from-customer-edge setup. Contract will specify which model they pick.
Leo Alvarez: Flag: Guaranteeing static public IPs we manage means reserved address allocations, routing constraints, and operational on-call for L3 changes. It’s non-trivial.
Maria Chen: Current private/on-prem guidance recommends customer-managed egress. If we offer Redwood-managed static egress as a paid add-on, we need runbooks, monitoring, and a billing model.
Sam Patel: Legal: if it’s written into the MSA we need precise failure modes and remediation SLAs. Absolute permanence across major infra migrations is risky. We should limit guarantee scope and include escape clauses.
Priya Shah: OK — proposal for PRD acceptance criteria:
- Customer chooses one of two modes at sign: CUSTOMER_EGRESS or REDWOOD_MANAGED_EGRESS.
- CUSTOMER_EGRESS: customer provides ASN, prefix list, BGP neighbor config; Redwood validates BGP session and test routes in staging.
- REDWOOD_MANAGED_EGRESS: customer signs an egress addendum; customer provides allowed destination CIDRs; Redwood allocates static Elastic-NAT IPs and documents cost pass-through.
Ryan Kim: Technical acceptance checklist to gate launch:
1) BGP session establishes (if CUSTOMER_EGRESS) and routes propagate for test prefixes.
2) For REDWOOD_MANAGED_EGRESS, static IPs show stable NAT in 3x consecutive deploy cycles.
3) TLS end-to-end verification to customer endpoints.
4) KMS integration validated for keys used in that tenant.
5) Performance smoke tests (latency, p50/p95) under expected QPS.
Leo Alvarez: Edge cases we must capture in PRD:
- Mixed-mode traffic: some tenants require customer egress for sensitive flows while others use Redwood-managed egress. Need clear routing precedence rules and config toggles.
- Failover behavior: if customer egress flaps, define whether we fail closed (drop) or fail open to Redwood-managed egress (only if configured).
- IP reassignment windows: acceptable maintenance windows where static IPs may be moved — documented and require customer opt-in for short windows.
Maria Chen: Operational model:
- First-90-days runbook: onboarding checklist, daily traffic sanity checks, 24/7 paging routing for critical egress failures.
- Ownership: Eng-platform owns BGP config artifacts pushed on behalf of customer; Ops/Infra owns runtime and NAT appliances; Customer Success coordinates customer-side tasks.
Sam Patel: Contract language suggestions:
- Define "IP Persistence": Redwood guarantees IP persistence unless affected by force majeure, major network provider outages, or mutually agreed maintenance.
- Include notice periods: 30-day notice for any planned maintenance that may affect IP assignment.
- Customer indemnity for firewall changes they control.
- Availability remedies: credits limited and capped; do not include unlimited indemnity.
Priya Shah: Sales asked whether Redwood will update customer firewall rules if routing fails. Short answer: we provide detailed change requests and a test harness, but customer performs changes on their edge.
Ryan Kim: Action items for PRD authoring (assigned):
- Draft "Connectivity Handoff Checklist" section (Ryan) with minimal required artifacts: ASN, allowed prefixes, BGP PSK optional, TLS cert chain, KMS key IDs, health-check endpoints.
- Draft operational escalation and first-90-days runbook (Maria).
- Draft addendum template and indemnity/maintenance language (Sam).
- Cost model and billing flow for Redwood-managed NAT (Leo).
Priya Shah: Can engineering + legal + sales review the draft by EOW? Reply with :white_check_mark: if you can.
Ryan Kim: @Maria Chen @Leo Alvarez @Sam Patel — pinging for Friday review. :white_check_mark:
Maria Chen: :white_check_mark:
Leo Alvarez: I can review technical ops and cost model. :white_check_mark:
Sam Patel: Will draft contract appendix; need the initial technical wording. :white_check_mark:
Priya Shah: Great. I will book a 30min sync Friday to finalize wording and ownership.
Ryan Kim: One more thing — include an automated failover test in the PRD: simulate blackhole of customer egress and verify that configured fallback behavior (drop vs failover) executes and is observable in logs/metrics.
